legacy_delta: Legacy: logging is session-scoped via `logging/setLevel` (sent once); server emits `notifications/message` at/above that level for the rest of the session. Modern (2026-07-28): `logging/setLevel` is REMOVED; client opts in per-request via `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel"]`; logs for a request ride that request's SSE response stream; omitting the meta key means no logs (by design).

Legacy: resource subscriptions via `resources/subscribe`; updates via `notifications/resources/updated`. Modern: subscriptions via `subscriptions/listen` (filter: `resourceSubscriptions` + `resourcesListChanged` opt-in), confirmed via `notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged`; long-lived stream with reconnect by re-sending `subscriptions/listen`.

Legacy: Tasks gated on `capabilities.tasks`; `tasks/list` + `tasks/get` (poll) + blocking `tasks/result` to fetch payload; `tasks/cancel` to cancel. Modern: Tasks are an extension `io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks` (SEP-2663), gated on negotiated extension not capabilities; `tools/call` returns `CreateTaskResult` (`resultType: "task"`); no `tasks/list`; only `tasks/get` polling; completed task inlines result (`resultType: "complete"", no blocking `tasks/result`); `input_required` state surfaces embedded elicitation, answered via `tasks/update` with `inputResponses`.

Modern-only: Multi-round tool results (MRTR) — a `tools/call` can return `input_required` embedding elicitation/sampling/roots-list; client answers and retries `tools/call` under a fresh JSON-RPC id until `complete`.

Legacy pattern `collect_elicitation` (server-to-client request via `server.elicitInput`) errors on a 2026-07-28 (modern) connection because server-to-client requests aren't allowed there; MRTR is the modern replacement.

Modern-only headers/errors: SEP-2243 `x-mcp-header` tool annotation causes Streamable HTTP client to mirror an argument into `Mcp-Param-*` request header; invalid header name (not RFC 9110 token) => tool MUST be dropped from `tools/list` by a conforming client. New JSON-RPC error codes for the modern era: `-32020` HeaderMismatch, `-32021` MissingRequiredClientCapability, `-32022` UnsupportedProtocolVersion (data.supported / data field lists server's supported versions), `-32601` Method not found (also present pre-2026 generically). `-32602` Invalid params also used, generic across eras but Inspector differentiates "Unknown Tool" vs "Invalid Parameters" presentation only in modern era UI (wire code identical both eras).
Legacy HTTP: server-assigned session id `Mcp-Session-Id` header; client tears down with HTTP `DELETE`. Modern: sessionless, per-request; no session id, so disconnect is purely local with no `DELETE`.

Deprecation: `notifications/message` (the whole legacy protocol-level logging mechanism) is deprecated as of protocol version 2026-07-28, remains available during a deprecation window; servers now expected to use per-request `_meta` opt-in logging or OpenTelemetry/stderr instead.

`server/discover` method and its response fields (`capabilities` incl. `extensions`, `instructions`, `supportedVersions`) and result `_meta` key `io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo` are new/modern-era additions used for protocol compatibility checks, replacing implicit legacy `initialize`-only negotiation.

methods.name: server/discover
methods.params: None documented in these pages beyond being a probe call (no args shown).
methods.result: capabilities (including extensions), instructions, supportedVersions; serverInfo (name/version) delivered in result _meta under key io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo.
methods.capability_gate: None required to call; used by clients before/instead of initialize to check protocol compatibility.
methods.notes: Debugging doc: 'Verify protocol compatibility: call server/discover to see which protocol versions the server supports.' Inspector protocol-eras doc: probed only when protocolEra is 'auto' (probe then fallback to initialize on non-modern outcome) or 'modern' (pinned to 2026-07-28, no fallback). Default era is 'legacy' which does plain initialize with no probing at all -- a debugging tool per the Note 'must not auto-probe'.

methods.name: initialize
methods.params: Not detailed beyond generic JSON-RPC initialize; CLI --method initialize takes no companions.
methods.result: CLI table: {serverInfo, protocolVersion, capabilities, instructions} for a connect-only probe.
methods.notes: Used in legacy era as the sole connect-time negotiation (no discover probe).

methods.name: tools/list
methods.result: list of tools; per SEP-2243, a tool with an invalid x-mcp-header annotation (not a valid RFC 9110 token) MUST be dropped from the list by a conforming client.
methods.notes: Inspector CLI --method tools/list; also --app-info variant emits NDJSON per tool reporting hasApp/resourceUri/csp/permissions without invoking tools.

methods.name: tools/call
methods.params: tool name + arguments; CLI requires --tool-name plus --tool-arg (coerced via JSON parse) or --tool-args-json (verbatim, no coercion); mutually exclusive.
methods.result: Normal result, or in modern era a CreateTaskResult (resultType: 'task') when run as a background task, or an input_required MRTR result embedding elicitation/sampling/roots-list request.
methods.capability_gate: Task execution gated by capabilities.tasks (legacy) or negotiated extension io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks (modern, SEP-2663).
methods.notes: isError:true in result still causes CLI exit code 5. -32602 Invalid params returned for unknown tool name or invalid params (era-independent wire behavior; Inspector UI in modern era distinguishes Unknown Tool vs Invalid Parameters presentation).

methods.name: resources/subscribe
methods.capability_gate: Legacy-era only mechanism per protocol-eras page.
methods.notes: Superseded by subscriptions/listen in modern era.

methods.name: subscriptions/listen
methods.params: a filter object carrying resourceSubscriptions plus a resourcesListChanged opt-in flag.
methods.result: long-lived stream; confirmed via notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged notification.
methods.notes: Client reconnects by re-sending subscriptions/listen if stream drops.

methods.name: logging/setLevel
methods.capability_gate: Legacy era only; 'modern servers opt in per request instead' -- method is gone/unused in modern era.
methods.notes: CLI table explicitly: 'Legacy era only; modern servers opt in per request instead.'

methods.name: logging/tail
methods.notes: CLI: 'Stream- or session-only methods (logging/tail, for example) are rejected [by the CLI], since a process that exits can't hold a stream open.'

methods.name: tasks/list
methods.capability_gate: Legacy era only (capabilities.tasks); no equivalent in modern era.
methods.notes: Modern era: 'there is no tasks/list, so Refresh re-polls the handles the client already knows about.'

methods.name: tasks/get
methods.result: task status/object; modern era full object shows resultType: 'complete' when done, inlined result.
methods.capability_gate: Legacy: capabilities.tasks. Modern: negotiated extension io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks (SEP-2663).
methods.notes: Used for polling in both eras; modern era is the only fetch mechanism (no tasks/result).

methods.name: tasks/result
methods.notes: Modern era has no blocking tasks/result call; result is inlined in tasks/get.

methods.name: tasks/cancel
methods.notes: Not explicitly restated for modern era in these pages.

methods.name: tasks/update
methods.params: inputResponses (answers to an embedded elicitation) for a task in input_required state.

methods.name: roots/list
methods.params: None documented beyond being invoked by server.filesystem example.
methods.notes: CLI note: '--method roots/set applies only to that one short-lived connection'; roots are otherwise only durably configurable via config file's roots field, advertised at connect. server-filesystem calls roots/list to learn allowed directories.

methods.name: roots/set
methods.notes: CLI-only ephemeral method; 'there is no roots flag' and this applies only to that one short-lived connection -- config file is the only durable way to set roots.

methods.name: servers/list
methods.result: list of servers in catalog, read without connecting.
methods.notes: CLI-only convenience method, not a wire MCP method to a server.

methods.name: servers/show
methods.result: server detail, with secret-bearing fields (env values, sensitive headers, OAuth client secrets) redacted; does NOT scrub credentials embedded in URL userinfo/query tokens or stdio args.
methods.notes: Warning: treat raw url and detail fields as sensitive before pasting into an issue/bug report.

methods.name: notifications/message
methods.params: level, data, logger name presumably (per generic logging notification).
methods.capability_gate: Legacy: sent for any request once client opted in session-wide via logging/setLevel. Modern: sent only for requests that stamped _meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel"]; server MUST NOT send it otherwise.
methods.notes: Deprecated as of 2026-07-28, remains available during deprecation window. Debugging doc: 'Servers must not send notifications/message for requests that omit this field' (the per-request _meta field).

methods.name: notifications/resources/updated
methods.notes: Triggers a 'last-updated' timestamp on the subscribed tile in Inspector UI.

requirements.text: Local MCP servers (stdio transport) must not log messages to stdout, as this will interfere with protocol operation.
All messages logged to stderr on stdio transport are captured by the host application automatically; this is the sanctioned logging channel for stdio servers.
Servers must not send notifications/message for requests that omit the io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel field in the request's _meta.
A server MUST NOT emit notifications/message for a request that did not opt in (modern era, per-request _meta stamping).
Clients should also include io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo in per-request _meta (in addition to the two required fields).
Every request must carry io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion and io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities in _meta.
A request missing either required _meta field (protocolVersion or clientCapabilities) is rejected with error -32602 (Invalid params).
If the server needs a client capability the request's clientCapabilities did not declare (e.g. elicitation), it returns MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError (-32021) naming the missing capabilities.
An UnsupportedProtocolVersionError (-32022) must list the server's supported protocol versions in its data field.
A conforming client MUST drop a tool with an invalid x-mcp-header annotation (SEP-2243) from tools/list.
Server-to-client requests (e.g. legacy collect_elicitation pattern using server.elicitInput) are not allowed on a 2026-07-28 (modern) connection; such calls error.

On stdio, the working directory for servers launched via a client's config may be undefined (e.g. '/' on macOS); configurations must always use absolute paths in config and .env files for reliable operation.

MCP servers launched over stdio inherit only a limited subset of environment variables automatically (platform-dependent); an explicit env key in client config is required to override/provide variables.

For Streamable HTTP transport, servers should use their own server-side log aggregation or OpenTelemetry for logs, since stderr is not captured by the client; standard HTTP tooling should be used to inspect requests/SSE streams.
requirements.cite: docs__2026-07-28__tools__debugging.md, 'Implementing logging > Server-side logging' (Streamable HTTP paragraph)

requirements.text: Claude Desktop (example client) requires a full quit-and-reopen (not just closing the window) to pick up server code changes.
Inspector launcher: passing more than one of --web/--cli/--tui fails with the exact message 'Specify at most one of --web, --cli, or --tui.'
requirements.cite: docs__2026-07-28__tools__inspector.md, 'Launcher flags vs. client flags' and configuration.md launcher table

requirements.text: Launcher mode flags (--web/--cli/--tui) must appear first on the command line; the first token not recognized as one of these ends launcher parsing and everything after is forwarded to the client unchanged.
requirements.cite: docs__2026-07-28__tools__inspector.md, 'Launcher flags vs. client flags' Note

requirements.text: Inspector CLI: --tool-arg and --tool-args-json are mutually exclusive.
Inspector CLI: on any non-zero exit, the CLI writes a single JSON line to stderr of shape {"error":{"code","message","status","url"}}.

Inspector CLI exit codes are fixed: 0 success, 1 usage/unexpected (catch-all), 2 no MCP App found (--app-info probe), 3 auth required (401/403, WWW-Authenticate, OAuth), 4 server unreachable (DNS/refused/timeout/fetch failed), 5 tool error (isError:true or tool not found).
A tools/call that returns isError:true still prints its payload but exits with code 5.
--app-info exit codes: tool with app exits 0, tool with no app exits 2, missing tool exits 5.
tools/list --app-info always emits NDJSON (one line per tool) regardless of --format; --format json only reshapes the single-tool tools/call --app-info output.
Without --use-stored-auth or --stored-auth-only, and with no TTY on stdin or stderr, the CLI fails fast with auth_required rather than hanging on an OAuth callback.
--stored-auth-only should be used in CI: never starts interactive OAuth or step-up, never auto-opens a browser; uses stored tokens or fails immediately with auth_required.
servers/show does not scrub credentials embedded in a server url (userinfo or query tokens) or in stdio args -- treat raw url/detail fields as sensitive.
Connections to remote HTTP/SSE servers honor HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY (and lowercase forms) and NO_PROXY; no Inspector-specific flag needed; proxy agent loaded lazily.
Web Inspector backend: never combine DANGEROUSLY_OMIT_AUTH and DANGEROUSLY_BIND_ALL_INTERFACES -- the backend spawns processes and holds OAuth tokens, so anyone reaching it can drive it.
Binding a wildcard host (0.0.0.0, ::, or equivalent) requires the explicit opt-in DANGEROUSLY_BIND_ALL_INTERFACES.

OAuth callback URL for CLI/TUI must be a loopback host (127.0.0.1 or localhost); the local callback listener receives the auth code over plaintext http, so any other host is rejected and there is no flag to override this.
requirements.cite: docs__2026-07-28__tools__inspector__configuration.md, 'CLI and TUI: OAuth client flags' table (--callback-url row)

requirements.text: --catalog and --config are mutually exclusive and neither combines with an ad-hoc target; passing both is rejected identically by all three clients.
A --config file is read-only: served as-is, never written, seeded, or migrated; a missing --config file errors (vs. --catalog which is created and seeded).
Default Inspector protocolEra should be 'legacy' (plain initialize, no probing) because a debugging tool must not auto-probe; 'auto' or 'modern' are deliberate opt-ins.
MCP defines eight RFC 5424 severity levels (debug through emergency) for logging.

wire_details: _meta key (request, client->server): io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel -- per-request log level opt-in (modern era). Value presumably one of the 8 RFC 5424 levels.
_meta key (request, client->server, required): io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion
_meta key (request, client->server, required): io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities
_meta key (request, client->server, should-include): io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo
_meta key (result, server->client): io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo -- name/version, delivered on server/discover response result _meta.

JSON-RPC error code -32602: Invalid params -- returned for a request missing required _meta fields, for unknown tool name ('Unknown Tool' panel in modern-era Inspector UI), and for other malformed inputs ('Invalid Parameters' panel).

JSON-RPC error code -32021: MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError -- returned when server needs a client capability absent from clientCapabilities; names missing capabilities. HTTP 400 in modern-era example (trigger_missing_capability tool).

JSON-RPC error code -32022: UnsupportedProtocolVersionError -- data field / data.supported lists server's supported protocol versions. HTTP 400 in modern-era example (trigger_unsupported_version tool).

JSON-RPC error code -32020: HeaderMismatch -- a required mirrored Mcp-Param-* header was missing or wrong (SEP-2243). HTTP 400 in modern-era example (trigger_header_mismatch tool). Note: Mcp-Param-* mirroring is skipped in browser/SDK environments (web Inspector client), so calling a mirrored tool from the web client omits the header and can trigger this against a strict server; CLI/TUI (Node) mirror correctly.
JSON-RPC error code -32601: Method not found -- HTTP 404 in modern-era example (trigger_method_not_found tool).
HTTP header: Mcp-Session-Id -- legacy Streamable HTTP server-assigned session id; client tears down session via HTTP DELETE. Not present/used in modern (sessionless, per-request) connections.
HTTP header family: Mcp-* -- standardized by the modern era per SEP-2243/SEP-2575; includes Mcp-Param-* (mirrored tool argument headers, e.g. city -> Mcp-Param-City) and Mcp-Session-Id.
HTTP status 401/403 with WWW-Authenticate header, or OAuth flow needed -- maps to Inspector CLI exit code 3 (auth_required).
CLI stderr JSON error envelope fields: error.code (string, e.g. "auth_required"), error.message, error.status (HTTP status, e.g. 401), error.url.

resultType enum values (Tasks / MRTR): "task" (CreateTaskResult from tools/call when run as background task), "complete" (final inlined task result), "input_required" (task or MRTR round awaiting more info, e.g. via tasks/update or a retried tools/call).
Extension identifier: io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks (SEP-2663) -- modern-era Tasks extension name, gates the Tasks feature via negotiated extensions rather than capabilities.tasks (legacy).

Tool annotation: x-mcp-header (SEP-2243) on a tool argument -- instructs Streamable HTTP client to mirror the argument value into a header named Mcp-Param-<Capitalized-Arg-Name>. Invalid header name (not a valid RFC 9110 token, e.g. containing a space) causes the tool to be excluded from tools/list.
Config/catalog JSON field: protocolEra, enum "legacy" | "auto" | "modern"; default "legacy".

Config/catalog JSON field: modernLogLevel, string level (e.g. "debug", "info", "off"); default "debug" per-server (Inspector opts into most verbose level by default since it's a debugging tool); "off" omits the logLevel _meta key entirely.
Config/catalog JSON server fields observed: type ("stdio"|"http"), command, args, env, url, headers, roots (array of {uri, name}), protocolEra, modernLogLevel.

Catalog default path: ~/.mcp-inspector/mcp.json (or MCP_CATALOG_PATH). CLI/TUI seed empty {"mcpServers": {}}; web backend seeds two sample stdio servers (filesystem-server-default via npx @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem /tmp; everything-server-default via npx @modelcontextprotocol/server-everything).
OAuth state file path: <MCP_STORAGE_DIR>/oauth.json; override via MCP_INSPECTOR_OAUTH_STATE_PATH (takes precedence over MCP_STORAGE_DIR).
Default OAuth callback URL: http://127.0.0.1:6276/oauth/callback (env override MCP_OAUTH_CALLBACK_URL / flag --callback-url), must remain loopback host.
Web backend default bind/ports: HOST default "localhost"; CLIENT_PORT default 6274; MCP_SANDBOX_PORT pins MCP Apps sandbox port (dynamic by default).

Web backend token env vars: MCP_INSPECTOR_API_TOKEN (pin session token), DANGEROUSLY_OMIT_AUTH (disable /api/* token check), ALLOWED_ORIGINS (comma-separated, replaces not merges default origin allow-list).
MCP_DEBUG / DEBUG env vars (launcher-level): append error stack to top-level failure; meaningful-value rule -- "0", "false", and empty string are treated as OFF.
MCP_AUTO_OPEN_ENABLED env var: "true" forces browser auto-open and allows OAuth prompts without a TTY; "false" never opens; unset opens only on a TTY.
Claude Desktop log file locations: macOS ~/Library/Logs/Claude/mcp*.log; Windows %APPDATA%\Claude\logs\mcp*.log.

Claude Desktop DevTools opt-in file: developer_settings.json with {"allowDevTools": true}, at ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/developer_settings.json (macOS) or %AppData%\Claude\developer_settings.json (Windows).
Inspector package name: @modelcontextprotocol/inspector, binary name mcp-inspector; requires Node >= 22.19.0.

Inspector CLI recognized --method values: initialize, tools/list, tools/call, resources/list, resources/read, resources/templates/list, prompts/list, prompts/get, logging/setLevel, servers/list, servers/show.
Inspector --format values: "text" (default, human pretty-print) | "json" (single JSON object on stdout, no banners).
sdk_implications: A PowerShell MCP server SDK MUST provide a stdio transport implementation that writes ALL log/diagnostic output exclusively to stderr (or an OTel exporter), and MUST make it structurally hard/impossible to accidentally write to stdout (e.g. redirect/guard the stdout stream, or force all cmdlet output/Write-Host equivalents away from stdout in stdio mode) since stdout is reserved for JSON-RPC framing.

Implement per-request logging opt-in for the modern era: read _meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel"] on each incoming request; only emit notifications/message (deprecated, transitional) when that key is present, and never otherwise. Provide a code path that instead ties emitted log entries to the current request's SSE/response stream when using Streamable HTTP.

Implement (or deprecate-but-support) logging/setLevel as a legacy-era-only handler; when operating in modern/2026-07-28 mode the SDK should not require or advertise this method as the log-level mechanism.

SDK must validate/require the two mandatory per-request _meta keys (io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion, io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities) on the server side and return -32602 Invalid params when missing; should also propagate/accept io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo.

SDK must implement server/discover (server-side handler and client-side caller) returning capabilities (incl. extensions), instructions, supportedVersions, and stamp serverInfo into the result's _meta under io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo.

SDK must implement typed errors: MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError (-32021) with a data field naming missing capabilities, and UnsupportedProtocolVersionError (-32022) with data.supported listing supported versions -- as distinct PowerShell exception/error types, not generic JSON-RPC failures, so callers can branch on $_.Exception type or error code.

SDK must implement HeaderMismatch (-32020) for SEP-2243 Mcp-Param-* header mirroring failures on Streamable HTTP transport; must validate x-mcp-header tool annotations as RFC 9110 tokens and exclude non-conforming tools from tools/list rather than erroring at registration time.

SDK must implement Tasks per era: legacy path exposing tasks/list, tasks/get, tasks/result (blocking), tasks/cancel gated by capabilities.tasks; modern path exposing tasks/get only (no tasks/list), tasks/update (for input_required responses with inputResponses), gated by negotiated extension io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks (SEP-2663), and tools/call must be able to return a CreateTaskResult (resultType: 'task').

SDK client must implement MRTR retry loop: when tools/call returns resultType input_required, resolve the embedded elicitation/sampling/roots-list request and retry tools/call with a fresh JSON-RPC id, with a configurable max-rounds guard (mirroring MRTR_MAX_ROUNDS) to avoid infinite loops.

SDK must implement modern subscriptions/listen (filter: resourceSubscriptions, resourcesListChanged) with server confirmation via notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged, and legacy resources/subscribe + notifications/resources/updated, selectable per protocol era; must support stream reconnect by re-issuing subscriptions/listen.

SDK's Streamable HTTP client must handle both legacy session semantics (Mcp-Session-Id header + HTTP DELETE teardown) and modern sessionless per-request semantics (no session id, no DELETE), selectable/auto-detected via protocol era negotiation, since a stateless modern handler cannot persist state between calls (important for any PowerShell in-memory server state design).

For a PowerShell Inspector-equivalent or test harness, mirror the exit-code/error-envelope contract if building a CLI test tool: exit codes 0/1/2/3/4/5 with the defined meanings and a single-line JSON error object on stderr, to be CI-scriptable in the same spirit as @modelcontextprotocol/inspector --cli.

SDK configuration loader (equivalent of catalog/config files) should support a protocolEra field (legacy|auto|modern, default legacy) and a modernLogLevel field (default debug, off = omit logLevel meta), and should default to NOT auto-probing (legacy behavior) to avoid disrupting silent legacy stdio test servers -- an explicit setting should be required to enable server/discover probing.

Any bundled interactive testing tool (PowerShell equivalent of TUI/CLI Inspector) should support --catalog (writable, seeded on first use) vs --config (read-only, errors if missing) semantics distinctly, and support a -- separator to pass through arguments to a spawned stdio server process.

OAuth/loopback callback implementation in any PowerShell client-side auth flow must restrict the callback host to loopback addresses (127.0.0.1/localhost) since the code is received over plaintext http.

Documentation/samples for the PowerShell SDK should instruct developers to always use absolute paths for stdio server command/args/env and .env files, given undefined working directory when launched by a host client, and to note that stdio servers inherit only a limited, platform-dependent environment variable subset unless explicitly configured.
open_questions: The exact request/notification schemas for server/discover, subscriptions/listen, tasks/get, tasks/update, and notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged (full parameter/result field lists) are not given in these five pages -- must be cross-checked against schema.ts/2026-07-28_schema.json for exact TypeScript/JSON Schema shapes before generating PowerShell classes.

The full list of RFC 5424 log levels (debug..emergency) is referenced but not enumerated in these pages verbatim -- confirm exact 8 level names and ordering from the logging spec page, not assumed here.

Whether -32602's distinct 'Unknown Tool' vs 'Invalid Parameters' presentation in the modern era corresponds to any wire-level distinguishing field (e.g. a data field) or is purely an Inspector UI heuristic based on message text is unclear from this page alone.

Exact shape of the CreateTaskResult object and the input_required task/MRTR result object (field names beyond resultType) is not given here; needs the tasks extension spec (SEP-2663) and schema files.

Not all of these pages define new_error code -32602 formally (it's described as generic/pre-existing); confirm against the full error taxonomy in the spec's basic/index or errors page for completeness.

The debugging.md page's Python/TypeScript logging examples use non-normative example package names (mcp.server.MCPServer, server.sendLoggingMessage) -- unclear if these map to canonical SDK APIs the PowerShell SDK should mirror one-to-one, or are illustrative only.
summary: These five pages cover MCP debugging practice and the reference Inspector tool for 2026-07-28. Debugging: stdio servers must log only to stderr (never stdout, which breaks framing); Streamable HTTP servers need external log aggregation/OTel since stderr isn't captured. notifications/message-based logging is deprecated as of 2026-07-28 in favor of per-request _meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel"] opt-in; servers MUST NOT send it otherwise. Connection troubleshooting requires server/discover (returns capabilities/instructions/supportedVersions, serverInfo in result _meta), and every request MUST carry _meta protocolVersion + clientCapabilities (else -32602), with -32021 for missing capabilities and -32022 (with supported versions in data) for version mismatch. Inspector: single package, three clients (web/CLI/TUI) sharing transports, config, OAuth state, and protocol-era negotiation. Protocol era (legacy/auto/modern) reshapes logging (setLevel vs per-request), subscriptions (resources/subscribe vs subscriptions/listen), Tasks (capabilities-gated tasks/list+tasks/result vs extension-gated tasks/get-only with inlined results), MRTR (modern-only elicitation/sampling retry loop), SEP-2243 header mirroring (Mcp-Param-*, -32020 HeaderMismatch), and session model (Mcp-Session-Id+DELETE vs sessionless). CLI client: --method-driven single-shot execution, strict exit codes 0-5 mapped to failure classes, single-line stderr JSON error envelope, --app-info NDJSON probing, CI-oriented --stored-auth-only. Configuration: launcher owns only --web/--cli/--tui and --help; --catalog (writable, seeded) vs --config (read-only, errors if missing) are mutually exclusive; extensive per-client flag/env-var tables including OAuth loopback-only callback constraint and dangerous web-backend flags that must never be combined.</summary>
